title: Longest Nice Subarray
key_insight: Nice subarray means pairwise AND of all elements is 0, which means the OR of window elements has no overlapping bits. Use sliding window with bitmask.
code_python3:
def longestNiceSubarray(self, nums):
    used = 0
    l = 0
    res = 0
    for r in range(len(nums)):
        while used & nums[r]:
            used ^= nums[l]
            l += 1
        used |= nums[r]
        res = max(res, r - l + 1)
    return res

title: Divide Intervals Into Minimum Number of Groups
key_insight: This is equivalent to finding the maximum number of overlapping intervals. Use a sweep line or sort start/end events.
code_python3:
def minGroups(self, intervals):
    events = []
    for l, r in intervals:
        events.append((l, 1))
        events.append((r + 1, -1))
    events.sort()
    res = cur = 0
    for _, delta in events:
        cur += delta
        res = max(res, cur)
    return res

title: Maximum Matching of Players With Trainers
key_insight: Sort both arrays and greedily match the smallest available trainer to the smallest player it can serve.
code_python3:
def matchPlayersAndTrainers(self, players, trainers):
    players.sort()
    trainers.sort()
    i = j = 0
    res = 0
    while i < len(players) and j < len(trainers):
        if trainers[j] >= players[i]:
            res += 1
            i += 1
        j += 1
    return res

title: Minimize Maximum of Array
key_insight: The answer is max of ceil(prefix_sum[i+1]/(i+1)) for all i, since we can only move values left.
code_python3:
def minimizeArrayValue(self, nums):
    ans = 0
    prefix = 0
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        prefix += x
        ans = max(ans, (prefix + i) // (i + 1))
    return ans

title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Arrays Similar
key_insight: Separate odds and evens, sort both arrays by parity groups, match greedily.
code_python3:
def makeSimilar(self, nums, target):
    nums_odd = sorted(x for x in nums if x%2==1)
    nums_even = sorted(x for x in nums if x%2==0)
    target_odd = sorted(x for x in target if x%2==1)
    target_even = sorted(x for x in target if x%2==0)
    ops = 0
    for a, b in zip(nums_odd, target_odd):
        ops += abs(a-b)
    for a, b in zip(nums_even, target_even):
        ops += abs(a-b)
    return ops // 4

title: Next Greater Element IV
key_insight: Use two monotonic stacks: first stack finds first greater, second stack finds second greater.
code_python3:
def secondGreaterElement(self, nums):
    n = len(nums)
    ans = [-1] * n
    stack1 = []
    stack2 = []
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        while stack2 and nums[stack2[-1]] < x:
            ans[stack2.pop()] = x
        tmp = []
        while stack1 and nums[stack1[-1]] < x:
            tmp.append(stack1.pop())
        stack2.extend(reversed(tmp))
        stack1.append(i)
    return ans

title: Minimum Addition to Make Integer Beautiful
key_insight: Greedily round up from lowest digit to reduce digit sum below target.
code_python3:
def makeIntegerBeautiful(self, n, target):
    def digit_sum(x):
        s = 0
        while x:
            s += x % 10
            x //= 10
        return s
    add = 0
    base = 1
    while digit_sum(n) > target:
        remainder = n % (base * 10)
        if remainder > 0:
            add_val = base * 10 - remainder
            n += add_val
            add += add_val
        base *= 10
    return add
